target_customer: Developer tool and API companies that want coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor to pick and correctly use their product
problem: Coding agents now decide which libraries and tools get installed in a codebase, and tool vendors have no way to measure or influence those picks, or to see what agents do with their MCP servers after install.
business_model: Managed service for agent discoverability plus self serve SaaS (MCP analytics and evals) with a free tier
product_category: Agent experience analytics and agent led growth for developer tools

founders.name: Theodore Otzenberger
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page: ex Palantir, founding engineer at Tsuga, a Datadog spin off, building observability infrastructure.

founders.name: Louis Scremin
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page and launch post: scaled AI agents and MCP servers at Joko, a consumer app with 6M users. Education not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Running real coding agents in a panel of sample repositories at scale, reconstructing MCP sessions and building an eval replay system is standard engineering with some hard parts; the company reported 17k runs in its first public study.

defensibility.rationale: Benchmark data on agent tool picks and the agent.reviews corpus could compound, but the measurement method and analytics features are copyable by observability and analytics vendors within months.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found as of Nov 2026; AgentCat, another agent experience platform, was reported in private beta around the same time.

market_need_then: Coding agents began choosing tools autonomously in 2025 and 2026, so vendors had a new distribution channel they could not measure. The company's own study and the agent.reviews site (100k+ reviews claimed) showed interest, but paying demand was not yet evidenced.

identity.logo: Uppercase ARMATURE wordmark in the site header
identity.visual_style: Developer tool aesthetic with sample dashboards
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct, short declarative lines such as Be the tool and Be the one they pick

branding.brand_signature: agent.reviews, a review site written by coding agents, framed by a founder as a G2 for agents
branding.community_and_virality: A Show HN for agent.reviews on 2026-10-07 reportedly reached 68 points and 49 comments; an earlier Hacker News study post on 17k agent runs is cited on the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Early and pre revenue; the agent.reviews launch earned some developer attention and press pickups, but the name itself is a common word and was not discussed in any source.

outcome_analysis: Armature is active and very young, with a Spring 2026 batch, a three person team in Paris and no confirmed exit. It rides the shift of tool selection to coding agents and has earned developer attention through original research and agent.reviews. Revenue, customers and funding are not verified in public sources, so the outcome is still open.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators (vcbacked, nordic9) list a $500K pre seed in May 2026 and a pre seed with Founders Future and French angels in July 2026, but no press release or company source was found, so no round is recorded. Competitor list left empty because no competitor source dated near the Spring 2026 batch was found; AgentCat (public beta slated Oct 2026) emerged later. Armature's own site describes a managed service; the dataset one liner mentions agent led growth for coding agents.
